key_safety.text: Adverse reactions were usually mild to moderate; the most frequent (≥0.5%) were headache (1.5%), nausea (1.2%), injection site reactions (0.6%), dysgeusia (0.5%) and feeling hot (0.5%). The most serious reactions are nephrogenic systemic fibrosis and hypersensitivity/anaphylactoid reactions.

detail.text: Boxed warning for Nephrogenic Systemic Fibrosis (NSF): GBCAs increase the risk for NSF among patients with impaired elimination of the drugs; NSF may result in fatal or debilitating fibrosis affecting the skin, muscle and internal organs.

citations.quote: WARNING: NEPHROGENIC SYSTEMIC FIBROSIS (NSF)

Gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs) increase the risk for NSF among patients with impaired elimination of the drugs. Avoid use of GBCAs in these patients unless the diagnostic information is essential and not available with non-contrasted MRI or other modalities. NSF may result in fatal or debilitating fibrosis affecting the skin, muscle and internal organs.

summary.text: Gadobutrol was approved as a new gadolinium-based contrast agent based on two confirmatory phase 3 studies (310123, 310124) demonstrating enhanced MRI visualization of CNS lesions and anatomy; the application was reviewed by the Peripheral and Central Nervous System Advisory Committee on January 21, 2011, which voted 16 to 0 to recommend approval, and was approved March 14, 2011.

citations.quote: Bayer HealthCare conducted two confirmatory phase 3 studies to support gadobutrol approval, each designed in a manner similar to those supporting the approval of other GBCAs. The study results demonstrated that gadobutrol enhanced MRI visualization of CNS lesions and anatomy.
The committee voted (16 to 0) to recommend gadobutrol approval.
Approval Date: March 14, 2011
